title: Austin Takes on Gas Pumps and Taxes
summary:
*   **Early Gas Station Regulations:** Approved a detailed permit for an underground gasoline tank and a curb-side pump on Congress Avenue, setting specific safety, lighting, and operational standards for this emerging automotive technology.
*   **Correcting Tax Errors:** Rectified an administrative error by canceling a personal property tax lien on specific lots that had been mistakenly assessed to a non-owner.
*   **Infrastructure & City Animals:** Authorized a 10-foot width adjustment for a section of Windsor Road and approved the humane destruction of a diseased and old city mule.
*   **New Driver Licensing:** Continued formalizing early transportation services by granting licenses to multiple "service car" drivers.

W A Barkley
Taxes
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Whereas,it appears from
examination of titles that W A Barkley did not on the 1st day of January ,1914, nor at any
other date,so far as has been made known to this Council ,own Lots 15 & 16,in Outlot 76
Division "D" ,North end addition of the City of Austin, Texas, but through error or
otherwise ,assessed said property on the rolls of 1914,as his own ; and Whereas, there are
certain property taxes yet owing by the said W A Barkley for the year 1914,and which said
taxes for personal propertyare in the nature of a lien or claim against said Lots 15 &
16,in Outlot 76 Division "D" and constitute an improper charge against the above described
property ,which is the property of W A Steen;
Now, therefore,
Resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That the Assesser & Collector of
taxes of this City be and he is hereby instructed to cancel and charge off as a debt or
lien against said Lots 15 & 16 Outlot 76 Division "D" any personal property or other taxes
that may appear as a charge thereon in favor of the said W A Barkley.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew & Powell 3 Absent excused, Councilmen Anthony & Haynes 2
Approved, A F Wooldridge,Mayor.

Councilman Powell offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of
the City of Austin, Texas : That the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements be ,and he is

J. C. Ross
Tanks
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Resolved by the City Council
of the City of Austin, Texas : That a permit be and is hereby granted to John C Ross to
install and maintain a 180 gallon Bowser Red Senty gasoline tank, to be approved by the
Supt of Police and Public Safety, under the sidewalk at 319- 321 Congress Avenue , Austin,
Texas. Resolved further: That in connection with this gasoline tank hereby authorized to
be installed, the said Jno C Ross is likewise authorized to install and maintain a
gasoline pumpto belocated at the curb line in front of 319- 321, Congress Avenue, at a
position to be designated by the the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements;said gasoline
pump to be of the most modern and approved construction and design, and subject to the
approval of the Supt of Police and Public Safety.
Resolved further :
That Jno C Ross shall install and maintain at the top and upon the gasoline pump hereby
authorized, an electric light of not less than 40 Watt power and placed in a globe of
notless than ten inches in diameter,which electric light must be kept illuminated not less
than three hours daily, between the hours of six and twelve O'clock P M . Resolved
further: That the hose through air, gasoline or any other oilor volatile substance is
conveyed, by pumping or otherwise, from the store house at 319-320 Congress Avenue, or
from the tank authorized to be placed in front of same, must be kept when not in actual
use, neatly coiled and stored, either in the receptaclein the sidewalk provided for such
hoseor in the receptacle in the pump authorized to be installedand provided for the
storing of said hose. Resolved further: That the work under this resolution authorized to
be installed and maintained must be installed and maintained ,where not otherwise
assigned, under the immediate supervision of the City Engineer of the City of Austin,
Texas, who is hereby authorized to prescribe nessary specifications for the work herein
authorized to be done.
Resolved further and finally:
That this permit is granted and must be accepted as revocable at any time in the pleasure
of the City Council.

October 14th 1915.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Resolved by the City Council
of the City of Austin : That the width of Windsor Road from the point of intersection of
the east line of said road with the south line of Enfield road to a point 338-2/10 feet
south be changed ten ( 10 ) feet by moving up the property line on the east side of said
roadbetween said above named points,for a distance of ten (10) feet towards the west.

Bartholomew & Powell 3
Absent Councilmen Anthony & Haynes 2
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
